abstract.text: National Journal of Physiology, Pharmacy and Pharmacology (NJPPP) is an open access, peer-reviewed, quarterly journal that publishes original research articles, review articles, case reports, and short communications in all areas of physiology, pharmacy, and pharmacology. The journal aims to provide a platform for researchers, academicians, and professionals to share their research findings and knowledge. NJPPP is committed to promoting high-quality research and maintaining ethical standards in publishing. The journal follows a rigorous peer-review process to ensure the validity and reliability of published work. It is indexed in various databases and is available both in print and online. The journal welcomes submissions from all over the world and encourages interdisciplinary research. The editorial board consists of experts from diverse fields who ensure the journal's scientific integrity. NJPPP is published by Mr. Sanjay Kataria and is based in India. The journal's ISSN is 2231-0541. For more information, please visit the journal's website.

evidence.quote: The Extended Mind
We propose to pursue a third position. We advocate a very different sort of externalism: an active externalism, based on the active role of the environment in driving cognitive processes.

thesis.text: The mind extends beyond the brain and body into the environment when external resources are actively coupled to cognitive processes, such that they function as part of the cognitive system.

sections.summary: The paper introduces the extended mind thesis, arguing that cognitive processes can extend beyond the brain into the environment when external resources are actively coupled to the agent.

sections.summary: The paper defines active externalism as the view that the environment plays an active role in driving cognitive processes, in contrast to passive externalism.
sections.title: Active Externalism Defined

sections.summary: The paper applies the extended mind thesis to cases of memory and belief, arguing that external resources like notebooks can constitute part of a cognitive system.

sections.title: Conclusion

sections.summary: The paper asks where the mind stops and the rest of the world begins, notes standard replies, and proposes active externalism, on which the environment plays an active role in driving cognitive processes.
sections.title: Introduction

source_span.end_text: Cognitive processes ain't (all) in the head!

sections.summary: The paper uses Tetris and related cases to argue that external resources can be part of cognitive processes, introducing epistemic action and the claim that cognitive processes are not all in the head.
sections.title: Extended cognition

source_span.end_text: Once we recognize that the crucial role of the environment in constraining the evolution and development of cognition, we see that extended cognition is a core cognitive process, not an add-on extra.

sections.summary: The paper defines active externalism as a coupled system whose external components play an active causal role, contrasts it with passive externalism, and discusses portability, evolution, and language.

sections.summary: The paper extends the argument from cognitive processing to belief, using the Inga and Otto notebook case to argue that beliefs can be partly constituted by environmental resources.
